newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Grounded Panama tanker headed for Argentina.
newsitem.headline: Grounded Panama tanker headed for Argentina.

text.p: A Panamanian-registered tanker which spilled 200 tonnes of oil off the Uruguayan coast is now sailing in international waters to the Argentine port of Bahia Blanca, Argentina's Coast Guard said Tuesday.
The San Jorge's cargo of 58,000 tonnes of crude has been transferred from the ship and it is sailing at low speed escorted by a tug boat, the Coast Guard said in a statement.
U.S. salvage firm Titan has been awarded the contract to deliver the San Jorge to a safe port.
Argentine oil firm ASTRA said last week it has an indirect 35 percent stake in the company that operates the ship, Transportes Maritimos Petroleros SA.
The San Jorge ran aground February 8, 20 miles (32 km) off the Uruguayan coast. It was on its way from the southern Argentine port of Comodoro Rivadavia to San Sebastian, Brazil.
Part of its oil washed ashore on the beaches of Punta del Este, a fashionable Uruguayan resort.
